# Study overview

Estimate the effects of PKH receipt on maternal healthcare using princeBART.
This alternative specification excludes district (`kabupaten`) from both the
model and the segmentation tree, allowing segments to reflect baseline household
characteristics. It uses the same sample, missing-value handling, and model
settings as [Analysis.qmd](Analysis.qmd). Removing district adjustment changes
the specification; this is an exploratory analysis of household heterogeneity.

# Dataset

```{r load-data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(princeBART)
  library(future)
  library(posterior)
})

load("processed_data.rda")
if (!all(c("hh_educ_baseline", "roof_type_baseline", "wall_type_baseline",
           "floor_type_baseline") %in% names(dat))) {
  stop("Regenerate processed_data.rda with preprocessing.qmd to use cleaned covariates.")
}
head(dat, 5)
```

- **Outcomes:** `good_assisted_delivery` (doctor or midwife attendance) and
  `delivery_facility` (delivery at a health facility).
- **Treatment:** `pkh_by_this_wave`, household ever received PKH by 2013.
- **Instrument:** `L07`, original randomized rollout assignment.
- **Predictors:** baseline household-head education and occupation; roof, wall,
  and floor categories; water, sanitation, and electricity; log household size
  and log per-capita expenditure; and numeric missingness indicators.
  Geographic identifiers and record identifiers are not predictors.

## Wall, floor, and private-latrine groups

| Category | Wall material | Floor material |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plastered masonry | Marble, ceramic, or terrazzo |
| 2 | Unplastered masonry | Tiles |
| 3 | High-quality wood | Cement or brick |
| 4 | Low-quality wood | High-quality wood |
| 5 | Bamboo or palm material | Low-quality wood |
| 6 | Zinc/metal sheeting | Bamboo or palm material |
| 7 | Not observed among baseline walls here | Earth |

- **`own_latrine_baseline = 1`:** private household latrine.
- **`own_latrine_baseline = 0`:** shared/public/no private latrine; also includes
  zero-filled missing values during fitting.

## Sample and model preparation

Keep the same sample as `Analysis.qmd`, including its geography availability
requirement, then remove `kabupaten` from the model data. For fitting, missing
factor values become a `Missing` level; missing numeric values are zero-filled
with missingness indicators. The loaded `dat` retains its original `NA` values.

```{r prepare-analysis}
baseline_controls <- grep("_baseline$", names(dat), value = TRUE)
required <- c("good_assisted_delivery", "delivery_facility", "L07",
              "pkh_by_this_wave", "kabupaten", "kecamatan")
model_dat <- dat[complete.cases(dat[required]), ] |>
  select(-kabupaten) |>
  droplevels()
for (variable in baseline_controls) {
  value <- model_dat[[variable]]
  if (!anyNA(value)) next
  if (is.factor(value)) {
    model_dat[[variable]] <- factor(
      replace(as.character(value), is.na(value), "Missing"),
      levels = c(levels(value), "Missing")
    )
  } else {
    model_dat[[paste0(variable, "_miss")]] <- as.integer(is.na(value))
    model_dat[[variable]][is.na(value)] <- 0
  }
}
baseline_controls <- grep("_baseline(_miss)?$", names(model_dat), value = TRUE)
baseline_controls <- baseline_controls[vapply(model_dat[baseline_controls],
  function(x) n_distinct(x) > 1L, logical(1))]
covariate_rhs <- paste(baseline_controls, collapse = " + ")
settings <- list(n_chains = 4L, workers = 4L, n_warmup = 500L,
                 n_samples = 750L, n_trees = 50L)
```

The common sample contains **`r nrow(model_dat)` delivery records** in
**`r n_distinct(model_dat$kecamatan)` subdistricts**. Instrument propensity is
estimated from the included household predictors. Multiple deliveries from a
mother remain; the likelihood does not adjust for subdistrict or mother-level
clustering, so credible intervals are not cluster-adjusted.

## Estimation and segmentation

Report posterior mean complier effects and 95% credible intervals in percentage
points. The segmentation tree chooses household predictors and has at most four
leaves, with at least 50 expected compliers per leaf. A single segment is possible
if the fitted effects do not support an admissible split.

```{r estimation-methods}
analyze_pkh <- function(outcome) {
  old_plan <- plan()
  on.exit(plan(old_plan), add = TRUE)
  if (settings$workers == 1L) plan(sequential) else plan(multisession, workers = settings$workers)
  set.seed(20261102)
  fit_ps <- prince_BART(
    as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", covariate_rhs, "| L07 | pkh_by_this_wave")),
    data = model_dat, uptake_type = "binary", n_chains = settings$n_chains,
    workers = settings$workers, n_warmup = settings$n_warmup,
    n_samples = settings$n_samples, n_trees = settings$n_trees, keep_trees = FALSE
  )
  plan(sequential)
  chains <- lapply(fit_ps$chains, function(chain) {
    pc <- 1 - chain$p_a - chain$p_n
    rowSums(pc * (chain$m_y1c - chain$m_y0c)) / rowSums(pc)
  })
  tau <- unlist(chains, use.names = FALSE)
  estimate <- tibble(
    Estimate_pp = 100 * mean(tau),
    Lower_pp = 100 * unname(quantile(tau, 0.025)),
    Upper_pp = 100 * unname(quantile(tau, 0.975))
  )
  draws <- as_draws_array(array(unlist(chains),
    c(length(chains[[1]]), length(chains), 1),
    dimnames = list(NULL, NULL, "Complier effect")))
  segments <- segment_heterogeneity(
    fit_ps, vars = baseline_controls,
    rpart_control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0, maxdepth = 2),
    min_compliers_bucket = 50, ci_level = 0.95, plot = TRUE
  )
  effects <- as_tibble(segments$effects) |>
    transmute(segment, Estimate_pp = 100 * mean,
              Lower_pp = 100 * ci_lower, Upper_pp = 100 * ci_upper,
              n, Expected_compliers = n_group)
  effect_plot <- segments$plot$effect +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) format(100 * x, trim = TRUE)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Complier effect (percentage points)", y = NULL)
  list(estimate = estimate,
       diagnostics = summarise_draws(draws) |> select(variable, rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail),
       effects = effects, plot = effect_plot)
}
```

# Objective 1: Skilled birth attendance

```{r assisted-delivery}
assisted <- analyze_pkh("good_assisted_delivery")
assisted$estimate
assisted$diagnostics
```

## Effect heterogeneity

```{r assisted-heterogeneity}
assisted$effects
assisted$plot
```

# Objective 2: Delivery at a health facility

```{r facility-delivery}
facility <- analyze_pkh("delivery_facility")
facility$estimate
facility$diagnostics
```

## Effect heterogeneity

```{r facility-heterogeneity}
facility$effects
facility$plot
```

Positive effects indicate increased use of maternal healthcare among households
whose PKH receipt was changed by rollout assignment. `n` counts delivery records;
`Expected_compliers` sums posterior complier probabilities. Factor levels retain
the authors' category indices; `Missing` and `_miss` splits describe data
availability. Household segments can also reflect geographic differences because
household characteristics and location may be correlated. These post hoc summaries
do not establish subgroup differences or account for selection of the tree.
